newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mostly up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mostly up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Friday on a technical rebound after successive falls in the past few days, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose to 13.07 precent from 11.00 percent on Thursday.
Total turnover fell to 7.70 million lots from 9.19 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
The rates had fallen earlier this week due to plunges on the domestic A share market due to Beijing's crackdown on the stock markets.
"The rise today was a technical rebound," said one trader. "Traders had expected the A share markets to continue to be weak next week and this limited the room for solid rises of the repo rates."
"Most of the repo rates had a slight rebound today, but the rise was slight with little buying evident due to the poor performance of the A share markets," said another trader.
The issue and listing of three new A share firms next week in Shanghai and Shenzhen should be a stimulus to push up early-maturing contracts, traders said.
